title: SLA-first launch playbook and experiment matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, SLA-first launch playbook and an experiment matrix for iterative rollouts. The emphasis is on measurable, observable gates tied to contractual or product SLA primitives so engineering, product-ops, and SRE can make consistent go/no-go decisions. This is intended to be a working notebook during the 30/60/90 activation window.

What makes this different:
- SLA-first: every decision gate maps to a single SLA or invariant (latency P95, error-rate, throughput, cost burn per 1k requests).
- Experiment-driven rollouts: traffic safepoints for A/B experiments and rapid rollback triggers baked into the matrix.
- Lightweight, owner-focused checklist for each gate: clear owner, CI test, smoke probe, monitoring query, and rollback command.

High-level cadence (30/60/90):
- Day 0–30: internal beta, 5–10% seeded traffic, primary goals: correctness, latency baseline, feature flag telemetry.
- Day 31–60: public beta, 10–40% traffic with staggered cohorts, primary goals: stability under load, SLO attainment, initial cost curves.
- Day 61–90: ramping to GA, apply autoscale tuning, finalize SLA language for customers, freeze experiment matrix.

Decision gates and mapped SLAs (examples):
- Gate A (internal beta start): no blocking customer-facing errors in 48h, P95 latency < 700ms on canonical prompt set, KV cache hit rate > 60%. Owner: Feature PM.
- Gate B (public beta ramp to 25%): 7-day rolling error-rate < 1.0%, sustained throughput within reserved capacity without queueing, cost per 1k tokens within 15% of forecast. Owner: Eng Lead.
- Gate C (GA readiness): 14-day SLO attainment (99.9% for availability tier), documented fallback model and region routing, documented runbook and SLA appendix. Owner: Product Ops Manager.

Experiment matrix template (fill per rollout):
- Experiment ID: EXP-YYMM-##
- Hypothesis: (one sentence)
- Metric primary: e.g., end-to-end success rate (E2E_R), latency P95, cost-per-request
- Guardrail metrics: error-rate, downstream queue length, customer-facing latencies
- Traffic fraction schedule: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% (timing per row)
- Stop condition: any guardrail exceeds threshold for X minutes/rolling window
- Rollback plan: exact command and who executes
- Owner and escalation chain

Sample thresholds (adjust per product):
- E2E_R: > 98.0% over 60 minutes
- Latency P95: < 900ms for latency-sensitive routes; < 2s for heavy batch routes
- Error-rate: < 0.5% customer-visible for GA routes (beta tolerance 1.0%)
- Cost drift: < 20% above forecast for initial 72h after ramp

Monitoring and probes (what to instrument before traffic increases):
- Smoke probe: synthetic canonical prompt that validates response schema + rag checks (run every 30s from three regions)
- Real-user sampling: 1% distributed sample with session IDs forwarded into telemetry buckets
- Model fallback probe: hit fallback routing and assert response time < fallback SLA
- Capacity probe: synthetic burst test to saturate a single Dedicated shard while observing queue length and token service time

Owner checklist per gate (copyable):
- Owner: name and backup
- CI: all unit/integration tests green, smoke pipeline passed in staging
- Rollout config: feature flag + percent + cohort list documented in experiment matrix
- Observability: dashboards created (latency, errors, cost, queue length) and runbook linked
- Stakeholder comms: email thread or doc update with expected ramp schedule and SLAs
- Runbook ready: step-by-step rollback commands and escalation phone list

Rollback & mitigation primitives (common patterns):
- Toggle feature flag to 0% for cohort (fastest)
- Re-route to lower-capacity but higher-availability model variant (e.g., half-precision quantized model)
- Throttle non-critical background requests and prioritize interactive traffic
- Expand emergency capacity (burst pool) if cost allows and error-rate is under control

Communication templates (concise):
- Pre-ramp note: purpose, owner, hypothesis, key metrics, expected user impact, start time window, rollback plan, on-call list
- Post-ramp summary: traffic fractions, metric deltas vs baseline, anomalies, next steps

Postmortem & learning loop:
- If any gate trips a critical SLA, a blameless mini-postmortem (48h) is required within 5 working days with action items and owners.
- Maintain a short changelog for experiment matrix and final SLA appendix for legal/commercial teams.

Appendix: quick commands and queries (examples to copy-paste):
- Query: rolling error-rate 60m: metrics.query("error_count / requests", window=60m)
- Query: latency p95 30m: metrics.query("latency_p95", window=30m)
- Command: toggle feature flag: infra-cli feature-flag set --name=my-feature --percent=0 --actor=owner
- Command: reroute to fallback model: router update --route=/chat --model=fallback-v1 --actor=oncall

Notes and open questions (working):
- Should the initial internal beta enforce a cost budget cap per team? Pros/cons to discuss w/finance.
- Do we require a separate 'privacy' gate for customers with sensitive datasets (private deployments)?
- Validate that experiment stop conditions are wired into the dispatch layer for automatic throttling if needed.

Next steps (for this draft):
- Confirm thresholds with SRE and Finance by EOD next week (owner: Priya).
- Wire smoke probe into staging Canary and document dashboard IDs (owner: Ethan).
- Run a dry-run of the rollback commands in test environment during the next maintenance window (owner: Marta).

Revision history:
- 2025-01-10: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-01-22: added sample thresholds and cadence (Ethan)
- 2025-02-02: updated owners and experiment template; moved to in_review (Priya)

End of doc.
